identity.title: From Text to Forecasts: Bridging Modality Gap with Temporal Evolution Semantic Space

problem.claim: Use textual information to improve time-series forecasting under event-driven non-stationarity.

gap.claim: Text describes temporal impacts implicitly and qualitatively, while forecasting models require explicit quantitative signals; existing methods reportedly over-attend to redundant tokens and struggle to translate semantics into numerical cues.

contributions.claim: TESS introduces a Temporal Evolution Semantic Space as an intermediate bottleneck between text and forecasting modalities.
The space represents interpretable, numerically grounded temporal primitives—distribution shift, volatility, shape, and lag—extracted by an LLM with structured prompting and confidence-aware gating.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish TESS by inserting a temporal semantic bottleneck composed of numerically grounded primitives between modalities.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In controlled semi-synthetic experiments, the authors report that existing methods over-attend to redundant tokens and do not reliably convert textual semantics into usable numerical cues.
On four real-world datasets, the authors report up to a 29% reduction in forecasting error versus state-of-the-art unimodal and multimodal baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Text may help forecasting with event-driven non-stationarity, but its qualitative temporal descriptions do not align with quantitative forecasting signals.
Controlled semi-synthetic experiments reportedly expose redundant-token attention and unreliable semantic-to-numeric translation in existing methods.
TESS bridges modalities through an intermediate space of grounded temporal primitives extracted and confidence-gated from text.
Experiments on four real-world datasets reportedly show up to 29% lower forecasting error than unimodal and multimodal baselines.

source_observation.claim: The paper maps qualitative text into a small set of interpretable temporal primitives before fusion, using structured prompting and confidence-aware gating.

lessons.interpretation: An explicit semantic interface can make cross-modal translation more inspectable and align representations with the downstream task.
lessons.application: For another multimodal forecasting problem, define task-relevant, numerically grounded intermediate primitives and gate uncertain extractions before model fusion.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when the domain lacks stable interpretable primitives or when discretizing rich semantics would discard essential information.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset identities, forecasting horizons, error metric, absolute errors, or whether the 29% reduction is consistent across all four datasets.
It does not report ablations isolating the bottleneck, primitive set, prompting, or gating contributions.
